title: The Crooked Scales of Obbrindle
story: In the salt market of Low Brinewall, Obbrindle the Salt Assessor taxes every cart with a different crooked rule, hoping nobody checks his arithmetic. A widow's cart of 240 salt bricks is about to be taxed into nothing. Mr 6 steps up with a chalk stub and asks to see the numbers.
question: Obbrindle first seizes 25% of the 240 salt bricks as a "weighing fee," then seizes 40% of whatever is left as a "road tithe." How many salt bricks does the widow keep?
solution: The weighing fee takes 240 x 0.25 = 60 bricks, leaving 240 - 60 = 180.
The road tithe takes 40% of 180, which is 72, so 180 - 72 = 108.
praise: Taking percents one at a time was the right plan — the second percent just had to come off the NEW pile of 180, not the original 240.
hint: Find what's left after the first fee, then take the second percent of that smaller pile — not of 240.
victory: Mr 6 chalked both subtractions right on Obbrindle's scale pan, and the crowd counted along out loud. The assessor turned the color of wet salt and handed back 108 bricks, plus a cart, plus an apology.
imagePrompt: A pale ledger-faced assessor in a salt-crusted robe scowling over brass scales in a bustling seaside salt market, while a small numeral-six knight chalks percentages on the scale pan to a cheering crowd.
